column5: Huck Bennett; Minki Hhan; Zihan Li; Noah Stephens-Davidowitz
column6: Lattices with Large Kissing Number from Local Density
column7: Let $κ_p(n)$ denote the maximum kissing number of a lattice $\mathcal{L} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that $κ_p(n) \geq 2^{Ω(\sqrt{n})}$ for all $p\ge 1$ and that $κ_p(n) \geq Ω(α_p^n)$ for all $p > 2$, where $α_p > 1$ is a constant depending only on $p$. In particular, our former result improves on the previously best known lower bound of $κ_2(n) \geq 2^{Θ(\log^2 n)}$ for the $\ell_2$ kissing number, which has stood for over $60$ years. (In concurrent and independent work, Laarhoven and Kominers [arXiv, 2026] showed a similar lower bound on $κ_2(n)$ using similar techniques.) In fact, our lower bounds follow from efficient (randomized) constructions of lattices with large kissing number. Our results use a general construction of lattices with large kissing number. Specifically, we show a simple equivalence between such lattices and a new object that we call an exact locally dense lattice. Closely related objects appear throughout the literature on computational lattice problems. Our constructions of lattices with large kissing number then follow as corollaries by showing that constructions due to Bennett and Peikert [RANDOM, 2023] (using Craig lattices) and Aggarwal and Stephens-Davidowitz [STOC, 2018] (using sparsification of $\mathbb{Z}^n$) in fact give exact locally dense lattices, as well as a new construction of exact locally dense lattices built from rotations of the $m$-dimensional checkerboard lattice $D_m$.

column6: Schauder and Riesz Bases for Higher-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces Inspired by ReLU Neural Networks
column7: Motivated by the role of piecewise linear functions in ReLU neural networks, we study systems of dilated functions in the Lebesgue spaces $L_q([0,1]^d)$, $q\in(1,\infty)$. For a sequence $τ\in\ell_1$ we consider the operator $T_τg(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty τ_k g(kx)$ and the function system $\mathcal Z^τ$ obtained by applying it to the trigonometric system. We show that $τ\mapsto T_τ$ is an isomorphism of algebras from $\ell_1$ with the Dirichlet convolution as multiplication onto an algebra of operators and connect the inverse of $T_τ$ to the inverse of $τ$ with respect to the Dirichlet convolution. We give explicit conditions on $τ$, under which the resulting system $\mathcal Z^τ$ is a Schauder basis of $L_q([0,1]^d)$ and, for $q=2$, a Riesz basis for which we estimate the Riesz constants in terms of $τ$. We characterise the Riesz bases of this type in terms of a sequence space of Dirichlet convolution multipliers, and we treat mixed systems of cosine and sine functions with different sequences. Finally, we apply these results to the system generated by two piecewise linear functions inspired by ReLU networks and improve the known lower Riesz constant to $2/3$, independently of the dimension.

column5: Stephan Ramon Garcia; Loïc Grenié; Ethan Simpson Lee; Giuseppe Molteni
column6: Bounds for the residue of Dedekind zeta functions under GRH and applications
column7: Let $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ be the residue at $1$ of the Dedekind zeta function of a number field $\mathbb{K}$. We prove explicit upper and lower bounds for $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH). Previous explicit bounds of comparable generality are weaker and require a weak form of Artin's holomorphy conjecture: our bounds improve the constants while assuming only GRH for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions. The new lower bound enables all imaginary quadratic fields with class number $\leq 2000$ to be detected (assuming GRH). Furthermore, we demonstrate that the upper bound can be significantly reduced when considering extensions of any fixed, nontrivial field.

column5: Mykola Pratsiovytyi; Yaroslav Vynnyshyn; Oleh Vynnyshyn
column6: A series with a Cantorval set of subsums and ratio of consecutive terms tending to $1/2$ (the second Jones problem)
column7: The second Jones problem (2011) consists in determining whether there exists a convergent positive series for which the ratio of consecutive terms has a limit and the set of subsums is a Cantorval; in the survey by Gł{\k a}b and Prus-Wiśniowski (2026) this problem is included in the list of open problems. In this paper, a family of such series is constructed explicitly as combinations of blocks of the form $\frac{2^k-1}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-1}}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-2}}{2^t} + \cdots + \frac{2}{2^t}$, where $t$ is the index of the last term of the block in the series and $k\ge2$ is the length of the block. For each series of the family it is proved that its set of subsums contains an interval and is not a finite union of closed intervals, and hence is a Cantorval. The proof relies on mixed-radix numerical systems with a redundant alphabet and uses an idea of Guthrie and Nymann (1988). If the lengths of the blocks tend to infinity, then the limit of the ratio of consecutive terms of such series is $\tfrac{1}{2}$, which, by a result of Jones, is the only possible value of the limit for which the set of subsums of a series can be a Cantorval. Thus, an affirmative answer to the second Jones problem is obtained.

column6: On the calculation of an integral introduced by Hubert Delange
column7: In his paper, ''Sur la distribution des fractions irréductibles de dénominateur $n$ ou de dénominateur au plus égal à $x$'', Hubert Delange considers the family integrals defined by \begin{equation*} \int_0^1\left(\frac{N(n,t)}{φ(n)}-t\right)^{2q}dt, \end{equation*} where $n>1$ and $q>0$ are positive integers, $φ$ is the Euler totient function, and for any real number $t>0$, $N(n,t)$ counts the number reduced fractions whith denominator $n$ that belong to the interval $]0,t]$. He was able to evaluate the integral for $q=1$ but stated that ''Malheureusement, nous n'avons pas su jusqu'à présent faire cette évaluation pour $q>1$''. In addition to its intrinsic interest, this calculation would help understand the asymptotic distribution of the $φ(n)$ totatives of $n$ relative to $φ(n)$ equidistributed numbers in $[0,n]$. In this paper, we first provide some general properties of the integral for any $q>1$ and reduce the problem to its calculation for odd square-free integers with at least two distinct prime factors. We then analyse into more detail the case $q=2$ for which we provide a formula that reduces the problem to the evaluation of the fourfold Möbius sum, of integer valued modular sums related to generalized Dedekind sums.

column5: Eva Bayer-Fluckiger; Stevell Muller; Matthias Schütt
column6: Dynamical degrees of automorphisms of non-projective hyperkähler manifolds
column7: We determine the dynamical degrees of bimeromorphic automorphisms of hyperkähler manifolds of all known deformation types with irreducible characteristic polynomial.

column6: The Tate Conjecture for Ordinary Calabi-Yau Threefolds
column7: We use the theory of canonical lifts to prove the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi-Yau threefolds over finite fields, and also for divisor classes on certain ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties.

column5: Rotem Kalisch; Tali Monderer; Elyasheev Leibtag; Shachar Weinbaum; Michael Shalyt; Ido Kaminer
column6: An Infinite Family of Apéry-like Recurrences for Euler's Constant
column7: Euler's constant $γ$, also known as the Euler-Mascheroni constant, remains one of the most elusive constants in mathematics. Despite extensive study, its irrationality is still unproven, and Apéry-like approximations of it are remarkably scarce. We present a novel identity that expresses $γ$ in terms of a Meijer G-function and its first few derivatives. This identity is then generalized and used to systematically generate infinitely many Apéry-like approximations of $γ$ using a Conservative Matrix Field construction based on the Meijer G-function.

column6: Counting with Hiccup Sequences
column7: The $(0,x,1,2)$-hiccup sequence starts at $x$ and increases by 1 when the current index has already appeared as a value, and by 2 otherwise. We prove directly that for $x\geq3$ the gaps between its missing values are $1,2,3,\ldots$, each repeated $x-2$ times, and we derive closed formulas, an explicit error bound, and a generating function in terms of Ramanujan's theta functions. The counting functions of the complements satisfy nested recurrences. The sequences of missing values are the partial complements of polygonal numbers. In particular, the $(x-2)$-fold composition of the enumeration of the positive integers that are not $x$-gonal is the hiccup sequence minus 1. We extend the nested recurrence and a tree interpretation to every miss increment $z\geq2$ and every initial value $x\geq2$. Further interpretations involve polyomino vertices, monochromatic pairs, and, by a theorem of Bickle, Ramsey core numbers.

column5: Felipe Gonçalves; João P. Ferreira; Maksym Radziwiłł
column6: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
column7: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.

column6: On the saturability of $p$-adic Lie groups
column7: Lazard theory is becoming increasingly important in $p$-adic representation theory, especially when studying mod $p$ representations. For $G$ a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $K/\mathbb Q_p$, a question going back to Lazard is when a pro-$p$ Iwahori subgroup of $G(K)$ admits a saturated $p$-valuation. In this article, we establish a deep connection to Moy-Prasad theory, and show that the Moy-Prasad filtration defines a saturated $p$-valuation on $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$ for any point $x$ in the semisimple Bruhat-Tits building of $G$, given a mild assumption on the maximal torus of $G$ and that $p>2$. We also compute Lazard Lie algebras defined over $\mathbb Z_p$ and the polynomial ring $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$ associated to the saturated group $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$, which allows us to reinterpret the Moy-Prasad isomorphism as an isomorphism of Lie algebras over $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$.

column5: Martin N. Huxley; Matthew C. Lettington; Karl Michael Schmidt
column6: On Divisor Function Polynomials and Dirichlet Series
column7: We find the Dirichlet series and convergence bounds for the counting function of sum systems (collections of sets of non-negative integers whose Minkowski sum is an arithmetic progression). This motivates the definition and study of divisor function polynomials, which are generating functions for the non-trivial divisor function and for the balanced divisor function that counts, up to a sign, non-trivial ordered factorisations into squarefree factors. These divisor function polynomials turn out to be intimately connected between each other and with Bernoulli numbers and ordered Bell polynomials.

column6: Weighted, GIT and Néron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
column7: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the Néron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted Néron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For binary sextics we prove the explicit inequality $h_{\inv}\le h_{\text{GIT}} + \frac{1}{2} \log 302$, with nonnegative local differences at the finite places that vanish at places of good reduction. We then construct a family of semistable binary sextics over $E\times E$, where $E:y^2=x^3-2$, whose relative Jacobian carries a section of infinite order, and we show that the Jacobian over the base point is absolutely simple. Along every curve in the parameter space through the base point, the Néron--Tate height of the section is a positive multiple of the weighted moduli height up to an error of square-root size, and up to a bounded error when the curve is rational. As applications, we obtain explicit families of genus-two Jacobians of positive rank over $\mathbf{Q}$, an infinite congruence lattice of fibres of positive height, and canonical-limit formulas along elliptic curves in $E\times E$.

column6: On a conjecture on Romanoff type representations
column7: Let $r_1,\ldots,r_t$ be positive integers, and let $\mathcal A$ be the set of integers of the form $2^{k_1^{r_1}}+\cdots+2^{k_t^{r_t}}$, where $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ are positive integers. For any positive integer $n$, let $r(n)$ be the number of representations $n=p+a$ with $p$ an odd prime and $a\in \mathcal A$. We prove that if $r_1^{-1}+\cdots+r_t^{-1}=1$, then, for every fixed positive integer $m$, the set of integers $n$ with $r(n)\ge m$ has positive lower asymptotic density. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Chen.

column5: A. Alvarez Cruz; E. A. Alvarez Gutierrez
column6: Regularization of a Divergent Arithmetic Product via the Asymptotic Monoid: The Case of $(-1)^{ω(n)}$
column7: We apply the generalized monoid of words and logarithmic-prefix functionals of \cite{C1} to the regularization of the divergent product \[ P_ω=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{(-1)^{ω(n)}}, \] where \(ω(n)\) is the number of distinct prime divisors of \(n\). The associated Dirichlet series \(D_ω(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{ω(n)}n^{-s}\) has a natural boundary at \(\Re(s)=0\), as established by Meretov (1987) and recovered here as a special case of the Estermann--Dahlquist theory of Euler products, which makes zeta regularization impossible: the derivative \(D_ω'(0)\) does not exist. This product therefore lies completely beyond the reach of classical regularization methods. We construct the canonical net encoding the sign sequence, define the logarithmic-prefix functional with exponent \(α=2\), and extract a finite value through the weighted evaluation functional of the monoid framework. The evaluation functional is shown to converge absolutely, and this convergence is unconditional: it follows from the classical zero-free region of \(ζ(s)\) (de la Vallée Poussin), which yields the effective bound \(T_ω(x)=O(x\,e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}})\) for some \(c>0\). Numerical computation up to \(N=10^7\) gives the regularized value \[ P_{ω,\mathrm{ren}}\approx 0.7731, \] a new constant of arithmetic origin that cannot be obtained by any classical summation method. We also compute the second derivative of the Dirichlet series at \(s=1\), \[ D_ω''(1)=8\,C_2\ln 2, \] where \(C_2\) is the Hardy--Littlewood twin prime constant, which provides an unconditional analytical link to the arithmetic structure of the sequence \((-1)^{ω(n)}\). A self-contained proof of the natural boundary, based on the Estermann--Dahlquist theorem, is given in Appendix~A.

column6: Appell Sequences in Analytic Number Theory: Shifted Expansions and Dirichlet L-Functions
column7: We place the Appell shift theorem for asymptotic expansions inside a Borel--Laplace framework and apply it to two classical functions of analytic number theory: the Hurwitz zeta function \(ζ(m,q)\) and the Lerch transcendent \(Φ(z,m,a)\). The resulting shifted expansions have coefficients given by Appell polynomials evaluated at the shift, with remainders controlled uniformly on compact sets. The generating sequences are identified explicitly in terms of the Taylor coefficients of the Borel kernels. In a second direction, we extend the Appell--Mellin framework of Navas, Ruiz and Varona to Dirichlet \(L\)-functions. For a primitive non-principal character \(χ\) modulo \(q\), we construct an explicit Appell--Mellin generating function \(A_χ(t)\) whose associated Appell sequence satisfies \(R_n^χ(x) = L(-n,χ,x)\), and we prove the functional equation \(A_χ(t) = χ(-1)A_χ(-t)\). We further establish five structural properties of the polynomials \(R_n^χ\): identification with generalized Bernoulli polynomials, a difference equation, an explicit formula, a Fourier expansion, and the trivial zeros of \(L(s,χ)\). To the best of our knowledge, these results do not appear in the literature.

column6: Campana strong approximation on generalized Markoff surfaces
column7: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.

column6: Sharp Bounds for Limits of $N$-Point Correlation
column7: We consider the question which functions $f$ may appear as limiting functions of the $N$-point correlation. We obtain sharp point-wise lower and upper bounds. The explicit examples constructed to show the sharpness of the bounds are based on van der Corput sequences.

column6: Additive complements to the primes and large gaps between Romanoff numbers
column7: We prove that every set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ for which $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ contains all sufficiently large integers satisfies $B(X)\gg\log X\log\log X$, where $B(X)=\#(\mathcal{B}\cap[0,X])$ and the implied constant is absolute. This proves a quantitative form of Ruzsa's Conjecture 2 and gives a negative answer to the $O(\log X)$ question in Erdős Problem 32. The bound follows from a more general result: for an arbitrary set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and sufficiently large $X$, we construct a block of $\lfloor c\log X\log\log X/(B(X)+1)\rfloor$ consecutive integers in $[X/2,X]$ outside $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$, provided this length is positive. As an application, we obtain $G_{\mathcal R}(X)\gg\log\log X$ for the longest block in $[1,X]$ containing no Romanoff number $p+2^n$, improving the bound $G_{\mathcal R}(X)\gg\log\log X/\log\log\log X$ of Kalmynin and Konyagin. The argument also applies to $p+a^n$ for every fixed integer $a\ge2$. The key step is a lemma on large shifts, proved using truncated products of divisor sums and the removal of auxiliary primes dividing differences of shifts.

column6: Short Recurrences and Straight-Line Programs for Primes
column7: We give a short autonomous recurrence that generates every odd prime, in increasing order, from the single initial value $8$. Its integer state determines both its output and its next update: the lowest set bit gives the next prime, while the highest set bit determines the sieve period. The same state also determines the following prime gap. A related recurrence represents the prime-counting function as the $2$-adic valuation of a single integer. Independently, a direct packing of a finite divisor sieve yields fixed arithmetic constructions for the $n$-th prime, the prime-counting function, and the twin-prime counting function. We express these constructions as straight-line programs using addition, truncated subtraction, multiplication, integer division, exponentiation, and remainder. Counting operations with reuse of computed values gives programs of lengths $166$, $132$, and $167$, respectively; one autonomous recurrence update uses $99$ operations. Explicit arithmetic subroutines remove all auxiliary operations, including bitwise AND. The programs unfold into fixed arithmetic terms without variable-length sums, products, or searches.

column6: Thurston's Legacy at the Interface of Surface Dynamics, Train Tracks, and Arithmetic
column7: In this chapter, we discuss the interaction between low-dimensional dynamics, symbolic dynamics, and geometric topology, focusing on the algebraic characterization and asymptotic behaviour of stretch factors or equivalently pseudo-Anosov dilatations. We first review the algebraic foundations linking Perron--Frobenius theory, multi-variable Euclidean algorithms, and Lind's characterization of topological entropy for shifts of finite type, emphasizing recent constraints on the Perron--Frobenius degree of expansion constants. We then relate these dynamical invariants to the combinatorial world, examining train tracks for surfaces and automorphisms of free groups. Finally, we briefly review the relevance of fibered 3-manifolds, detailing how the Thurston norm, Fried's concavity theorem over fibered cones, and McMullen's Teichmüller polynomial come into play.

column6: Hecke modules associated to certain ternary lattices of half-discriminant $p^2$ and $4p^2$
column7: We consider Hecke modules of orthogonal modular forms attached to definite ternary lattices of half-discriminant $p^2$ with $p$ prime and $4p^2$ with $p$ an odd prime. Where possible, we prove explicit Jacquet-Langlands style correspondences with spaces of classical modular forms (in the spirit of Birch and Hein-Tornaria-Voight), and give conjectures for the remaining genera. This is done by applying sequences of Watson-style transformations that reduce the discriminant while preserving the adelic orthogonal group.

column6: On the Quantitative Bounds of Nonlinear Roth Theorem
column7: We prove that any subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ lacking non-trivial polynomial progressions $(x, x + y, x + y^2)$ satisfies $\lvert A \rvert \le CN \exp\bigl(-c(\log \log N)^β\bigr)$ for effective absolute constants $C, c, β> 0$. The argument develops a density increment framework localized to anisotropic quadratic Bohr sets. To handle mixed linear and quadratic frequencies, we establish a multilinear transference principle coupled with a relative quadratic inverse theorem based on Balog--Szemer{é}di--Gowers additive energy rigidity. Boundary stability across increments is maintained via semi-algebraic model regularization using cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Cauchy--Crofton estimates, while dimension growth is controlled by dissociated basis reduction and multidimensional Erd{ő}s--Tur{á}n--Koksma equidistribution.

column5: Hargun Bhatia; Yashi Jain; Casey Perdue; Ben Savoie
column6: Higher mod $p$ Satake transforms: explicit formulas and images for $\mathrm{GL}_2$
column7: Heyer's left adjoint to derived parabolic induction gives rise to higher mod $p$ Satake transforms \[ \mathcal S_V^i: \mathcal H_G(V) \longrightarrow \mathcal H_M\bigl(H^i(K_U,V)\bigr), \] whose extreme degrees recover Herzig's invariant and coinvariant transforms. For $G=\mathbf G(F)$, where $\mathbf G$ is a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$, we describe these maps explicitly using Mackey decompositions and corestriction in group cohomology. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, we evaluate them on the standard Hecke generators, showing that their support lies in a single Weyl orbit and that their values on the individual support cosets are concrete corestriction operators. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, we determine the image in every cohomological degree for each non-Steinberg Serre weight. The endpoint images are the classical polynomial Satake images, while every interior image is of the form \[ k[x,y^{\pm1}]/(x^r) \] for some positive integer $r$. Thus, every interior image is a finite nilpotent thickening of the Laurent polynomial algebra $k[y^{\pm1}]$. We give explicit bounds for its thickness, prove that they are sharp, and show that in the unramified case every interior image is either reduced or a square-zero thickening.

column6: Real Fiducial Vectors Only Exist in Dimensions $d\equiv 3 \pmod{4}$
column7: We investigate restrictions on the dimensions and coordinate fields of real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors. Our main result is that such vectors can exist only in dimensions $d\equiv 3\pmod{4}$. This result is motivated by evidence showing that real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors can exist only in dimensions $d = 4m^2 + 3, m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. We further restrict the possible dimensions when the coordinate field is a totally real number field, an even or odd degree extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, a real quadratic field, or a maximal real subfield of a cyclotomic field. Lastly, we establish non-existence over odd-degree number fields under either positivity of all non-trivial cyclic-shift overlaps or a conjectural containment of a distinguished quadratic field in the SIC field.

column6: Towards linear growth for biprojective hypersurfaces of small dimension
column7: After removing suitable thin subsets, we count rational points of bounded height on some hypersurfaces of small bidegree in $\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^3$ and in $\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^2$. One of the ingredients is a new estimate for the number of rational points of bounded height on diagonal quadratic surfaces which improves as the coefficients grow.

column6: Stieltjes constants for Hurwitz-type L-series attached to periodic arithmetic functions
column7: We investigate generalized Stieltjes constants attached to Hurwitz-type Dirichlet series of the form $$ L(s, f, x)=\sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{f(n)}{(n+x)^s} $$ where $f$ is a periodic arithmetic function and $x\in\mathbb C\backslash\{0,-1,-2,\dots\}.$ We prove that these series admit meromorphic continuation to the whole complex plane, with at most a simple pole at $s=1$. We further derive functional equations satisfied by $L(s,f,x).$ Our main result gives an explicit formulas of the Stieltjes constants $γ_n(f, x)$ appearing in the Laurent expansion at $s=1$. In particular, we obtain explicit evaluations in the case of rational $x$. As an application, we derive explicit closed-form expressions for the first three generalized Stieltjes constants associated with nonprincipal real primitive odd Dirichlet characters arising from quadratic fields. These expressions are given in terms of the class number of the corresponding quadratic number field. These results extend and unify recent work of Blagouchine and others on generalized Stieltjes constants and Hurwitz-type $L$-functions.

column6: Khintchine dichotomy for images of self-similar measures and almost random walks
column7: Following the celebrated breakthrough in Bénard-He-Zhang, we prove Khintchine dichotomy for push-forwards of self-similar measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under uniform $C^{1+α}$ maps. For this, we also study almost random walks on $\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{Z})$ and prove their effective equidistribution.

column5: Shamil Asgarli; Sarthak Dassarma; Dragos Ghioca; Simon MacLean; Evan Stokdyk
column6: Covering plane curves over finite fields with lines
column7: We prove that, for every fixed $d\geq 2$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the $\mathbb{F}_q$-points of a geometrically irreducible reflexive plane curve of degree $d$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ can be covered by at most $\left(\frac{1}{d}+\varepsilon\right)q$ many $\mathbb{F}_q$-lines, provided that $q$ is sufficiently large. The same conclusion holds for $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible curves that are not geometrically irreducible, since they have only $O(d^2)$ $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. In particular, for sufficiently large $q$, the bound applies to every $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible plane curve of degree $d$ when $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)>d$. Our bound is asymptotically sharp. The proof combines Entin's Chebotarev density theorem for varieties over finite fields with the Pippenger--Spencer theorem on covers of nearly regular hypergraphs.

column6: The order types of the supports of $p$-adic algebraic Hahn series
column7: Let $p$ be a prime number. In 1986, David Lampert asked if one expands a $\mathbf{Q}_p$-algebraic number as a $p$-adic Hahn series, then what is the possible order type of its support? In 2001, Kedlaya made a vague conjecture that the possible ordinals can only be finite ordinals, $ω$ and $ω^ω$, where $ω$ is the first infinite ordinal. In this article, we solve Lampert's problem by confirming Kedlaya's intuition. Moreover, we completely characterize the $\mathbf{Q}_p$-algebraic numbers with order type of support at most $ω$. As an application, we determine the bi-algebraic set of the $p$-adic shadow map.

column5: Dijia Chen; Bowen Gan; Chao Qin; Yang Zhou
column6: Hecke Eigenform Product Identities for Full-Level Hilbert Modular Forms
column7: We study full-level Hilbert Hecke eigenform product identities over totally real fields of degree at least two, allowing arbitrary compatible narrow class characters. Combining our results with previous work, we classify products of two Eisenstein eigenforms of positive parallel integral weights and products of an Eisenstein eigenform of weight at least two with a cuspidal eigenform of positive parallel integral weight. The unique identity in each of these two classes is given by $E_{4}=60 E_{2}^{2}$ and $h_{8}=120 E_{2} \cdot h_{6}$, respectively, both over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$. The proofs use constant-term comparisons, indecomposable Fourier exponents, integrality of reciprocal Eisenstein constant terms, and a Rankin-Selberg formula for Petersson inner products. In the remaining case of a weight-one Eisenstein factor and a cuspidal factor, we also establish $h_5=12E_1(1,\varepsilon)\cdot h_4$ over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt3)$, where $\varepsilon$ is the nontrivial narrow class character. All eigenforms in these identities have unit-ideal coefficient one.

column5: Rachita Guria; Prahlad Sharma; Saurabh Singh
column6: On Quadric Surfaces Weighted by Arbitrary Coefficients
column7: For a non-singular quadratic form $F$ in four variables, we study integer solutions to $F=0$ with an arbitrary weight attached to one of the variables. This allows us to investigate genuinely sparse subsets of the corresponding variety. Our main input is to obtain cancellation in sums of character sums over the moduli arising in the application of the DFI's delta method to the quadratic hypersurface. This cancellation relies crucially on the equidistribution of quadratic roots and the Weil bound for Kloosterman sums.

column5: Yuval Amit; Lucas Chen; Christopher Housholder; Joshua Im; Joshua Khan; Steven J. Miller; Mateo Palomares; Devayani Pradhan
column6: Product and Quotient Set Dominance in Finite Groups
column7: A classic problem in additive number theory asks whether a given subset of integers has more sums or differences. This inquiry naturally extends to finite groups, where one compares the sizes of the product set $AA$ and the quotient set $AA^{-1}$ for a subset $A \subseteq G$. A finite group is considered product-dominant if it contains a higher proportion of subsets where $|AA| > |AA^{-1}|$, and quotient-dominant if the reverse is true. We establish statistical criteria to determine the dominance behavior of large finite groups by analyzing the moments of the random variable $d(A) := |AA| - |AA^{-1}|$. By translating product and quotient relationships into graph-theoretic constructions, we compute these moments through counting independent sets. Our main result demonstrates that for a growing sequence of finite groups $G_k$ with center size $Z_k$ and involution count $T_k$, the condition $Z_k = o(T_k)$ implies the groups are eventually product-dominant. Conversely, if $T_k \cdot \sqrt{3}^{R_k/Z_k} = o(Z_k)$ (where $R_k$ denotes the number of elements whose square is central), the groups are eventually quotient-dominant. Using these asymptotic conditions, we resolve the Miller--Vissuet conjecture by proving that all dihedral groups $D_n$ for $n \geq 3$ are product-dominant. Furthermore, we classify the dominance behavior of several major families of groups, proving that symmetric groups and non-abelian finite simple groups are product-dominant, while groups of odd order and certain abelian groups are quotient-dominant. Finally, for groups that fall outside our asymptotic conditions, we derive an explicit formula for the first moment utilizing the irreducible characters and conjugacy classes of the group.

column5: Qiang Huo; Zhengxing Lian; Kangbo Ouyang
column6: Odd order cases of Chowla's averages over arbitrary rectangles
column7: Let $λ$ be the Liouville function. In this paper we prove an average form of Chowla Conjecture for even $k $. that is, for every fixed even integer $k\geq 2$, we prove that \[ \lim_{\min\{M,N\}\to \infty}\frac{1}{MN}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{n=1}^Nλ(m)λ(m+a_1n)\cdotsλ(m+a_kn)=0. \] We construct a stationary model for both averaging variables, derive the finite conditional-entropy estimates. A comparison of overlapping intervals on the logarithmic axis then forces this function to vanish.

column6: On the Imaginary Part of $ζ'/ζ$
column7: We derive an explicit zero-side formula for the imaginary part of a smooth truncation of the logarithmic derivative of the Riemann zeta-function. The resulting kernel is the odd companion of the Fejér kernel in Montgomery's pair-correlation identity. Motivated by the recent breakthrough of Anthropic's Claude \cite{Claude26}, we also give an expository account of how the real-part identity can be turned into a matrix problem, overcoming the clustering obstruction for zeros off the critical line. Finally, we discuss how the new imaginary-part identity may contain additional information about such clustering.

column5: Alex Burgin; Anastasios Fragkos; David Kruzel; Michael Lacey; Amelia Stokolosa
column6: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
column7: Given an integer $k \geq 2$, there are integers $M_k$ and $P_k$ so that for all $A \subseteq \mathbb F^n_p$ does not contain a restricted polynomial progression of the form \begin{align*} x, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n \end{pmatrix}, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^2 \\ y_2^2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n^2 \end{pmatrix}, \ldots, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^{k-1} \\ y_2^{k-1} \\ \vdots \\ y_n^{k-1} \end{pmatrix}, \end{align*} where $x \in \mathbb F^n_p$, with $p>P_k$, and $y \in \{0,2, 3, \ldots, M_k\}^n \backslash \{\vec{0} \}$, for some fixed $M_k$, then $A$ must have density bounded above by $\frac{C}{(\log^{(k^{O(k)})} n)^c}$, where $C, c>0$ only depend on $k$ and $p$. For $k\geq 4$, the best previously known bound came from the density Hales--Jewett theorem and was of inverse Ackermann type. The proof uses a recent inverse theorem for noise stability of Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer, which arose in the study of constraint satisfaction problems. The main new ingredient is a proof that the underlying distribution counting restricted polynomial progressions does not admit a nontrivial abelian embedding, by way of an involved algebraic argument. Reasonable bounds are provided for $P_k$ and $M_k$.

column6: Reciprocal LCM powers and Robin's criterion
column7: For $κ> 1$, we study the reciprocal LCM-power function \[ σ^{[κ]}_{-1}(n) := \sum_{d \mid n}μ(d)\,σ_{-1}(n / d)^κ. \] We determine its average and extremal orders. A natural Robin-scale normalization is strictly increasing in $κ$ and tends to $σ_{-1}$, yielding an RH-equivalent criterion. Unconditionally, the corresponding Robin inequality holds eventually on every bounded parameter interval. Directed interval arithmetic proves the inequality for each $n > 5040$ and $1 < κ\le 100{,}000$.

column6: A conditional bound $Λ\le0.13963$ for the de Bruijn--Newman constant
column7: Assuming that $ζ(s)$ has no nontrivial zero with $\mathrm{Re}\, s > 7/8$, as asserted in a recent unrefereed preprint of OpenAI, we obtain $Λ\le 13963/100000 = 0.13963$ for the de Bruijn-Newman constant. A published Polymath boundary computation supplies a finite-region strip of half-width $1/5$. We derive an approximation on $3 \le \mathrm{Im}\, z \le 6$ from its general Riemann-Siegel coefficient bounds. At height $61/20$, a fixed cutoff permits two differentiations, and comparison with $ζ$ bounds both the zero-density kernel and its vertical derivative. A new conjugate-pair inequality and a twenty-four-step strip comparison give the stated bound. The finite scalar and polynomial certificates are included in the paper; earlier comparisons giving $0.17973$, $0.17172$, and $0.16408$ are retained to show the source of the gain. The argument uses neither Gordon's analytic inputs nor Gomila's new computations. The seven-eighths hypothesis remains an assumption, and the published numerical boundary input is retained.

column6: A Rigid Analytic Curve Can Have a Dense $p$-adic Orbit
column7: Let $\mathcal D$ be a product of Drinfeld upper half spaces and let $J$ be the corresponding product of projective linear groups acting on $\mathcal D$. We prove that if $Y$ is a reduced, quasi-compact separated strict $\mathbb C_p$-analytic space and $f: Y\to\mathcal D$ is analytic with $\dim Y<\dim\mathcal D$, then $J f(Y(\mathbb C_p))$ is closed and nowhere dense in $\mathcal D(\mathbb C_p)$. The quasi-compactness assumption is necessary even when the source is a strict rigid analytic curve, while a quasi-compact perfectoid source can still have an orbit closure with nonempty interior. For every finite extension $F/\mathbb Q_p$ and $d\geq3$, we construct a closed smooth irreducible non-quasi-compact curve in $Ω_F^{d-1}$ with dense orbit under a fixed diagonal one-parameter subgroup. We also construct a $\mathbb Q_p$-defined analytic map from the open unit disc to $\mathbf P^2$ with dense $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit, and an analytic map from a one-dimensional affinoid perfectoid torus to $\mathbf P^2$ whose $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit closure has nonempty interior.

column6: Polynomial parametrization of $\text{SL}_2$ over global function field rings
column7: We combine the universal polynomial matrix identities of Larsen--Nguyen with Trost's arithmetic lemmas to obtain polynomial parametrizations of $\text{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ for every global function field $K$ and every nonempty finite set of places $S$. The additional ingredient is a function-field cancellation lemma, proved using ray class fields and Chebotarev in odd characteristic and the perfectness of finite residue fields in characteristic two. The proof also gives a polynomial matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$ that works simultaneously for all these rings.

column6: Hankel Matrix Decompositions and Digital Sequences over Function Fields
column7: This paper studies formal Laurent series, with particular emphasis on their continued-fraction and Laurent-series expansions. Knowledge of both expansions is important, for example, in the study of Kronecker-type sequences in uniform distribution theory and in the search for potential counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of formal Laurent series. Our approach investigates Hankel matrices over a field and relates them to Laurent-series expansions over the same field. We describe such matrices via a block $\mathcal{L}\mathcal{B}\mathcal{U}$ decomposition, using recursive algorithms based on the continued-fraction coefficients of the corresponding Laurent series. The upper-triangular factor $\mathcal{U}$ has several remarkable properties. In particular, it is constructed columnwise from the so-called Ostrowski-type representations of powers of $X$. Applying $\mathcal{U}$ in Niederreiter's digital construction yields an Ostrowski-type van der Corput sequence that can be related to the corresponding Kronecker-type sequence. For ordinary Kronecker sequences, such a relation is known in only one case, that of the $(n\varphi)$-sequence. The original motivation for our study of Hankel matrices was to recast the search for counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of Laurent series as the search for specific Kronecker-type sequences. Interestingly, the method developed for the study of Kronecker-type sequences also allows a new perspective on the celebrated Sobol' construction. Our approach yields a short and elegant proof of its excellent distribution properties.

column5: Nihar Gargava; Matthias Gröbner; Michael Simkin
column6: A cyclotomic gluing construction for lattice sphere packings
column7: For a positive integer $d$, let $Δ_d^L$ denote the supremum of the densities of lattice sphere packings in $\mathbb R^d$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large $d$, $Δ_d^L \gg d^2\log\log d\,2^{-d}$. Abuya-Gargava-Zhao obtained the same bound along a sparse sequence of dimensions by combining Venkatesh's cyclotomic symmetries with Klartag's stochastic ellipsoid method. We introduce a multi-cyclotomic gluing construction that allows this argument to work in every sufficiently large dimension.

column6: Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
column7: We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N\geq4$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta--Iovita--Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard--Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao--Liu. When $p$ has a unique prime of $F$ above it, we remove this hypothesis and obtain unconditional properness, by establishing base-change compatibility for spaces of overconvergent Hilbert modular forms and analyzing the associated spectral variety over certain closed subspaces of the weight space.

column6: On $m$-fullness in number fields
column7: We prove asymptotic formulas for the number of $m$-full ideals of bounded norm in a given ideal class and for the number of $m$-full algebraic integers of bounded Weil height.

column6: Geometrically Abelian Sections on Higher-Dimensional Varieties
column7: We investigate how much arithmetic information about a variety can be detected by sections of the geometrically abelian fundamental groups of sufficiently small open subvarieties. Over a \(p\)-adic field, such a section determines a rational point on the Albanese torsor, and, under a conjectural assumption, this point is represented by a \(0\)-cycle of degree \(1\) on the original variety if the variety has index \(1\). For curves, the latter statement holds unconditionally. Over finitely generated fields, such sections still force the relative Brauer group to vanish away from the characteristic. The key input is an identification of the Chern class obstruction attached to a section with the obstruction arising from local Tate duality. As a byproduct, we give a new proof of an open-subvariety strengthening of a theorem of Esnault and Wittenberg.

column6: Two Primes and Five Mixed Fibonacci-Lucas Summands
column7: Using the circle method, we prove that every sufficiently large positive integer is a sum of two primes, $u$ Fibonacci numbers and $5-u$ Lucas numbers for each $u\in\{1,2,3,4\}$. All recurrence indices are positive, and terms may be repeated.

column6: Improved zero-free half-planes for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
column7: Recently, a uniform $\frac{7}{8}$ zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and its transfer to Dirichlet $L$-functions was given by OpenAI in [Ope26a]. In its proof, there are several parameters $b=\frac{1}{8}, \ell=\frac{1}{6}$, and $κ$. In this paper, via varying $b$, $\ell$, and $κ$, following the same strategy, we slightly improve the bound $\frac{7}{8}=0.875$ to \[ B_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{18ξ_{\mathrm{new}}+7}{18ξ_{\mathrm{new}}+9} =0.874957019420098946\ldots, \] where $ξ_{\mathrm{new}}$ is the unique root in $(0.38858,0.38859)$ of $1188ξ^3-2160ξ^2+171ξ+190=0$. Explicitly, with $\arccos\in[0,π]$, \[ ξ_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{20}{33}+\frac{\sqrt{1391}}{33} \cos\!\left(\frac13\arccos\frac{28470}{1391^{3/2}} -\frac{2π}{3}\right). \] The limiting parameters are \[ \begin{gathered} b_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{8(3ξ_{\mathrm{new}}-1)(12ξ_{\mathrm{new}}^2-40ξ_{\mathrm{new}}+15)} {9(2ξ_{\mathrm{new}}+1)(24ξ_{\mathrm{new}}^2-20ξ_{\mathrm{new}}+5)}, \ell_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{5-6ξ_{\mathrm{new}}}{9+18ξ_{\mathrm{new}}},\qquad κ_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{18ξ_{\mathrm{new}}+5}{18ξ_{\mathrm{new}}+9} =2B_{\mathrm{new}}-1. \end{gathered} \] We also prove its optimality within the explicitly specified exponent comparison system. This result has been formalized by Lean [Liu26].

column6: On Igusa's conjectures for weighted homogeneous polynomials with isolated singularities
column7: In 1991, Denef introduced an explicit formula for Igusa's local zeta functions in terms of embedded resolutions of singularities over $p$-adic fields with good reduction. In this paper, by slightly generalizing the $p$-adic McKay correspondence given by the second author in 2017, we extend Denef's result to the setting of $\mathbb{Q}$-embedded resolutions of singularities. Consequently, the strong monodromy conjecture with respect to Igusa's local zeta functions holds for weighted homogeneous polynomials with isolated singularities. Moreover, we use our formula to prove Igusa's conjecture for exponential sums in the case of non-degenerate weighted homogeneous polynomials with isolated singularities.

column6: Twisted Jacquet modules and induction from Speh representations
column7: Fourier coefficients of Eisenstein series induced from Speh representations are the kernels of the generalized doubling method of Cai, Friedberg, Ginzburg and Kaplan. Ginzburg and Soudry integrated these coefficients against cusp forms to obtain Eisenstein series induced from shorter Speh representations and arbitrary cuspidal data. We determine the corresponding local modules over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. Let $q_F$ be the cardinality of its residue field. Let $J_s$ be the twisted Jacquet module of the representation induced from $Δ(τ,m+i)|\det|^s$. It carries an action of $G\times H$, where $G$ and $H$ are split symplectic or special orthogonal groups. Let $σ$ be an admissible representation of $G$ of finite length. We prove that $(J_s\otimesσ)_G$ is induced from $Δ(τ,i)|\det|^s$ and a fixed conjugate of $σ$, outside a finite set of values of $q_F^{-s}$ depending on $τ$ and $σ$. No genericity assumption on $σ$ is needed. For irreducible $σ$, this determines all irreducible quotients of $J_s$ of the form $σ^\vee\boxtimesπ$. The proof computes every orbit contribution, including those that vanish globally by cuspidality. It also gives an explicit finite set containing the exceptional parameters. This set is empty for irreducible supercuspidal $σ$ unless $G$ is the split group $\mathrm{SO}_2$. We prove the analogous result for the symplectic double cover. Over finite fields of large characteristic, we give the complete decomposition of the twisted Jacquet module when $τ$ is cuspidal on $\mathrm{GL}_n$ and $n$ is larger than the rank of $G$.

column6: A Complete Proof of Mueller--Ho Conjecture
column7: For $s>0$, and $z\in\mathbb H=\{z=x+iy:y>0\}$, define $θ(s;z)=\sum_{m,n\in\mathbb Z}e^{-πs\big(m^2y+\frac{(mx-n)^2}{y}\big)}$ and $ J(z;a,b)=\sum_{m,n\in\mathbb Z}e^{-π\big(m^2y+\frac{(mx-n)^2}{y}\big)} \cos\bigl(2π(ma+nb)\bigr)$ for the classical and shifted theta functions (Gaussian lattice sums), respectively. We prove that, up to the modular group, there exist three thresholds $0<α_a<α_b<α_c<1$ such that \begin{equation}\aligned\nonumber \Minima_{z\in\mathbb H,\,(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2}\Big(θ(1;z)+αJ(z;a,b)\Big)= \begin{cases} \;\big(e^{iπ/{3}};1/3,1/3\big), &\hbox{if}\;\; α\in[0,α_a),\\ \;\big(e^{iπ/{3}};1/3,1/3\big)\;\hbox{or}\;\big(e^{i{\varphi_{α_a}}};1/2,1/2\big), &\hbox{if}\;\; α=α_a,\\ \;\big(e^{i{\varphi_α}};1/2,1/2\big),\;\varphi_α\in(\varphi_{α_a},\fracπ{2}),\;\; &\hbox{if}\;\; α\in(α_a,α_b),\\ \;\big(i;1/2,1/2\big),\; &\hbox{if}\;\; α\in[α_b,α_c],\\ \;\big(iy_α;1/2,1/2\big),\; y_α\in(1,\sqrt3],\;\;y_1=\sqrt3,\;\;&\hbox{if}\;\; α\in(α_c,1], \end{cases} \endaligned\end{equation} where the complex variable $z$ and vector $(a,b)$, represent the total vortex shapes and relative positions of the two-component Bose gas, respectively. Consequently, this completely proves the conjecture of Mueller and Ho~\cite{Mue2002} (2002) arising in Bose--Einstein condensates.

column6: On $a^4+b^4+c^4+d^4=(a+27(b+c+d))^4$ and ten other new infinite families
column7: In 2008, Jacobi and Madden proved that $a^4+b^4+c^4+d^4=e^4$ has infinitely many primitive solutions with the linear relation $e=a+b+c+d$. We extend their result to relations with rational cubes $e=a+k^3(b+c+d)$ and prove infinitude for $k=3$ and $10$ other $k\ne 1$. We compile $30$ starting solutions. In the spirit of Jacobi and Madden's original paper, everything here is simple algebra except one theorem of Mazur.

column6: Geometric families of multiple elliptic Gamma functions and arithmetic applications, III
column7: This is the third paper in a series where we study arithmetic applications of the higher elliptic Gamma functions. In the first two articles in this series, we defined geometric families of these functions and proved that they satisfy coboundary and cocycle relations under the action of special linear groups and associated congruence subgroups. The main purpose of the present paper is to present a construction of conjectural higher elliptic units above number fields with exactly one complex place as special values of higher elliptic Gamma functions, upgrading the construction carried out by Bergeron, Charollois and García for complex cubic fields. These higher elliptic units are obtained by evaluating a multiplicative $(n-2)$-cocycle built from higher elliptic Gamma functions against a $(n-2)$-cycle associated to some group of totally positive units of a given number field of degree $n$ with exactly one complex place. We conjecture that these higher elliptic units are algebraic units which belong to prescribed abelian extensions of the base field where they are evaluated and that they satisfy a Kronecker limit formula which relates the logarithm of their modulus to values of derivatives of partial zeta functions at $s = 0$ in the base field. We showcase our conjecture on various examples for number fields of degree 3, 4 and 5.

column6: A uniform bound for the minimal degree of an isogeny between principally polarized superspecial abelian surfaces
column7: Let $p>3$ be a prime number. If $A$ and $B$ are two principally polarized superspecial abelian surfaces over $\mathbb{F}_{p^{2}}$ with $p^{2}$-Frobenius $[-p]$, we prove that there exists a separable polarized isogeny between them with multiplier at most $p/\sqrt{2}$. The multiplier bound is uniform in the pair and asymptotically optimal up to a small multiplicative constant. Given quaternionic coordinates, we provide a deterministic algorithm that satisfies this upper bound in polynomial time. For unrestricted multipliers, $\mathrm{KLPT}^{2}$ provides a heuristic algorithm with a multiplier upper bound of order $p^{6+o(1)}$ for arbitrary pairs and $p^{3+o(1)}$ when one polarization matrix is the identity matrix. Our algorithm's improvement is an explicit upper bound below $p$ with an unconditional deterministic guarantee.

column6: Rational curves on toroidal compactifications of Picard modular varieties
column7: It was known that the canonical bundle of a smooth toroidal compactification of a noncompact finite-volume ball quotient is nef in dimension $n\geq3$ and ample in dimension $n\geq6$. We prove that the canonical bundle is ample in dimension $n\geq4$ and show that this dimension bound is sharp. We construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular threefolds whose smooth projective toroidal compactifications have non-ample canonical bundle. Each compactification contains a smooth rational curve meeting the interior and having canonical degree zero. More generally, in every dimension $n\geq2$, we construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular varieties whose smooth toroidal compactifications contain smooth rational curves meeting the interior. In particular, such curves persist in arbitrarily high dimension, even when the canonical bundle is ample.

column6: Hyperplane winning for bad in manifolds
column7: We prove the hyperplane winning property of weighted badly approximable vectors inside nondegenerate analytic manifolds and affine subspaces satisfying almost optimal Diophantine conditions. This, in particular, answers a conjecture of Badziahin--Velani for higher-dimensional manifolds, including affine cases that were understood only in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

column5: Bartłomiej Bychawski; Bartosz Głowacki; Ivan Spyrydonov
column6: Further bounds in the polynomial Szemerédi theorem
column7: We show that there exists $c > 0$ such that any subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ having size $\gg N / \exp( (\log\log\log N)^c )$ contains a nontrivial pattern of the form $x,x+y,x+2y,x+y^3$. It is the first configuration of complexity strictly greater than $0$, other than refinements of arithmetic progressions, for which quantitative bounds over integers were obtained.

column6: Lie weights for CM curves and unipotent Selmer dimensions
column7: We prove an equidistribution result for Galois characters in the graded Lie components $L_n$ associated to the $\mathbf{Q}_p$-fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve $X$ over a number field $k$ with geometrically CM Jacobian. That is, we consider the $p$-adic completion of a fixed character lattice, where we define measures $μ_n$ counting normalized character multiplicities in $L_n$, and show that $(μ_n)_n$ weakly converges to the Haar measure. The key idea to prove convergence is to write the Fourier coefficients of $μ_n$ in terms of traces of operators on $L_n$ induced by symplectic operators on the Tate module, and control them with a known symplectic character formula, followed by Weyl's criterion for compact abelian groups. Our main arithmetic application is to combine equidistribution with the Iwasawa-theoretic method of Coates--Kim and a compactness argument for moving analytic loci, giving a dimension inequality for unipotent Selmer schemes: $\dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}H^1_f(G_{k,T},U_n)< \dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}\prod_{v\mid p}H^1_f(G_v,U_n)$ for all sufficiently large $n,$ with the quotient having limit superior at most $1/2.$ This answers a particular case of a conjecture by Kim, from which the finiteness of $X(\mathbf{Q})$ can be recovered when $k=\mathbf{Q}.$

column6: Uniform non-vanishing of prime quadratic twists of standard and symmetric square $L$-functions
column7: Let $S_k$ be the space of cusp forms of weight $k$ for ${\rm SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$, with $\dim S_k\geq1$, and let $χ_p=\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ for odd primes $p$. For fixed $s$ with ${\rm Re}(s)>(k+1)/2$, we prove that the proportion of primes $p\leq X$ satisfying $L(h,χ_p,s)=0$ tends to zero as $X\to\infty$, uniformly over nonzero $h\in S_k$. We also prove an analogous statement for nontrivial linear combinations of twisted symmetric square $L$-values of the normalized Hecke eigenforms when ${\rm Re}(s)>k$. The main ingredient of the proof is a non-concentration theorem for random Euler products under a pairwise local separation condition. As applications, we obtain spanning and density-one basis results in $S_k$ for the kernels associated with twisted standard and symmetric square $L$-functions, with explicit basis criteria in specified right half-planes when $\dim S_k=2$ or $3$. We show that almost every tuple of $\dim S_k$ primes gives a basis of $S_k^{\ast}$ from twisted periods at every noncentral critical index. We also prove a density-one result for rational bases of $S_k$ obtained from traces of Rankin-Cohen brackets of Eisenstein series at prime levels.

column6: Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers
column7: Let $p_i$ be the $i$th prime, and let $f(N)$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of \[ \left\{\prod_{i=1}^N p_i^{a_i}:0\le a_i<N,\ a_i\in\mathbb{Z}\right\} \] containing no two distinct legs of an integer right triangle. We prove \[ f(N) \ll N^N (\log\log N)^{-1/1296}. \]

column5: Alice Lin; Frank Lu; Jit Wu Yap
column6: Uniform Height Gaps in Arbitrary Characteristics
column7: We prove uniform height gaps for subvarieties of abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic, extending the new gap principle of Gao-Ge-Kühne. Our proof goes through the theory of adelic curves and globally valued fields, and proves the Bogomolov conjecture for an arbitrary globally valued field. This gives a different way to obtain uniform Bogomolov-type results, differing from the approaches of Dimitrov-Gao-Habegger-Kühne and Yuan. First, we prove the Bogomolov conjecture over globally valued fields for divisors. We then reduce the case of general subvarieties to the case of divisors by an induction argument. Specializing to the case of global function fields, we obtain a new proof of the geometric Bogomolov conjecture following the strategy of Gubler and Yamaki.

column6: Largeness of the wild locus
column7: We show that the wild locus of an étale morphism of smooth adic spaces over an affinoid field is either empty or contains a divisorial point. As a consequence, we establish the equivalence of curve tameness and valuation tameness without using resolution of singularities. Moreover, given a finite étale map of regular schemes $f \colon Y \to X$ that is curve tame over a base $S$, we construct a compactification $\bar{f} \colon \overline{Y} \to \overline{X}$ over $S$ that is numerically tame.

column6: Arithmetic Progressions in Midpoint Colourings
column7: We introduce an asymmetric variant of a classic problem by Roth about colourings of integers and midpoints. The new problem cannot be solved with the standard approach by Erdös-Sárközy-Sós which uses symmetry. We describe a Fourier Analytic approach which gives asymptotically tight bounds. In the $\mathbb{F}_3^n$ setting, the density increment we show is efficient and together with the Freiman-Ruzsa Theorem provides an affine subspace of near optimal codimension within the distinguished set. This approach adopted to the setting of the integers from $1$ to $N$ via Bohr sets and Bogolyubov-Ruzsa Lemma gives a progression of length being a power of $N$ which only depends on the number of colours. We then use Chang's Lemma and Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers Theorem to further improve the dependence on the number of colours.

column6: $q$-Analogues of some supercongruences related to Van Hamme's (E.2) and (F.2) supercongruences
column7: In this paper, we present a one-parameter extension of some supercongruences related to Van Hamme's $\mathrm{(E.2)}$ and $\mathrm{(F.2)}$ supercongruences. To deduce these results, we first establish the corresponding $q$-supercongruences modulo the third power of a cyclotomic polynomial. Our proofs rely on the \emph{creative microscoping} method devised by Guo and Zudilin~\cite{guo2019q}, together with Jackson's ${}_{6}φ_{5}$ summation formula.

column6: $q$-Supercongruences Modulo the Third and Fifth Powers of a Cyclotomic Polynomial
column7: In this paper, we establish several $q$-supercongruences for basic hypergeometric series modulo the third and fifth powers of a cyclotomic polynomial. These results extend several existing supercongruences related to the $\mathrm{(A.2)}$ and $\mathrm{(C.2)}$ supercongruences of Van Hamme. Our proofs employ the creative microscoping method developed by Guo and Zudilin \cite{guo2019q}, together with Watson's ${}_{8}φ_7$ transformation formula.

column5: Christoph Aistleitner; Siegfried Hörmann; Maryna Manskova
column6: On the asymptotic behavior of the number variance of random points on the unit torus
column7: The study of the distribution of real sequences in the unit torus has a long and rich history. There are many notions which describe the ``pseudo-random'' behavior of a given deterministic sequence (often of arithmetic origin), such as equidistribution (which describes the distribution on a ``global scale'') or the pair correlation (which is a ``local-scale'' statistics). Another popular and important statistics, which can be applied to all ranges from global via intermediate to local, is the number variance $V_N(s)$, which describes the mean-square fluctuation of the number of elements of an initial segment of the sequence in an interval of length $s$, when moving this interval around the torus. In the terminology of quantum chaology, where such statistics are used to describe the distribution of the energy levels of a system, pseudo-random behavior is called Poissonian behavior. Since the number variance is an important indicator to qualify pseudo-random behavior, it is quite surprising that the literature does not seem to contain a precise description of the distribution and of the almost sure asymptotic behavior of the number variance in the truly random case (i.i.d.\ random points), even in the comparatively simple setup of uniformly distributed points on the unit torus. In the present paper we calculate the distribution of the number variance with high precision throughout a wide range of the parameter $s$, and determine the precise threshold (in terms of $s$) where the ``Poissonian'' asymptotics $V_N(s) \sim N s$ breaks for a typical realization of a random sequence. Key technical input comes from the Komlós--Major--Tusnády theorem and the Karhunen-Loève decomposition.

column6: A Unified Framework for $p$-adic Congruences and $p$-adic Interpolations of Sequences
column7: In this paper, we treat the problem of determining when a sequence $\{c_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ with the exponential generating function $F(t)$ satisfies the congruence $c_{n+\ell p^k}\equiv c_n \pmod{p^{k+r}}$ for large $n$ and when its canonical interpolating functions are locally analytic. This type of congruence is often observed for several number-theoretic or combinatorial sequences, such as Bernoulli numbers, Euler numbers, and Fibonacci numbers. Traditionally, such congruences are proved by using $p$-adic integrations. In this paper, we present another approach to this problem. Instead of using $p$-adic integrals, we investigate an algebraic structure of the set of generating functions and establish some conditions on $F(t)$ that are equivalent to or sufficient for the congruence and smoothness of the interpolating functions. We also provide concrete applications of our framework to Genocchi numbers, generalized Euler numbers, and so on, which are outside the scope of the typical $p$-adic integration method.

column6: Continuity of the Julia sets in non-archimedean and hybrid settings
column7: Let $k$ be a complete, non-archimedean. We study the dynamics of families of one-variable rational functions parametrized by Berkovich spaces over $k$ and over $\mathbb{C}$ equipped with the hybrid norm. In both settings, we show an analogue of Mané--Sad--Sullivan's theorem about the continuity of the Julia set (in the Hausdorff topology). The non-archimedean case relies on the maximum modulus principle, which we show for analytic functions over analytic spaces without boundary.

column6: New Hoffman-type generators for alternating multiple zeta values
column7: We introduce multiple $s$ values and prove that every alternating multiple zeta value is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of multiple $s$ values $s(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ with $k_i \in \{1, 2\}$. We also study when certain multiple $s$ values can be expressed as $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combinations of multiple zeta values.

column6: Discorrelation of the Möbius function with linear phases in short intervals
column7: We introduce a new approach to studying correlations between arithmetic functions and linear phases with respect to highly irrational frequencies over short intervals. As an application, we prove that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H}μ(n) e(nα)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-1/3+\varepsilon } \] whenever $x^{0.58+\varepsilon }\leq H\leq x$. In the same range of $H$ we also show that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H} Λ(n) e(nα)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-A} \] for arbitrarily large $A>0$ unless there exists an integer $1\leq q\ll (\log x)^{O_A(1)}$ such that $\|qα\| \ll x (\log x)^{O_A(1)}/H^2$. This breaks the $3/5$ barrier in Theorem 1.5 of arXiv:1911.09076v2 and Theorem 2 of [T. Zhan, "On the representation of large odd integer as a sum of three almost equal primes," Acta Mathematica Sinica 7.3 (1991), 259-272]. Moreover, by our method, any improvement in large value estimates for character-twisted Dirichlet polynomials on the critical range would lead to a corresponding improvement in the lower bound for $H$.

column6: Invariant Measures on Smooth Algebraic Groups over Higher Local Fields
column7: We construct a positive, finitely additive, left-invariant measure on the congruence cylinder ring of a smooth $d$-dimensional algebraic group over an $n$-dimensional local field. The measure takes values in $\mathbb{R}((X_2))\cdots((X_n))$. A normalized cylinder of depth $(i_1,\ldots,i_n)$ has volume $q^{-di_1}\prod_{\ell=2}^nX_\ell^{di_\ell}$, where $q$ is the final residue-field cardinality. We also obtain coordinate-change and quotient integration formulas for this measure.

column6: Weak and genuine A_n-formality for number fields
column7: We introduce weak $A_n$-formality for Galois cochain algebras and, for profinite groups whose mod-$p$ cohomology is concentrated in degrees at most two, characterise weak and genuine $A_n$-formality through finite embedding problems and the projective system they form. We then study $A_n$-formality for number fields. Let $K$ be a number field and let $p$ be an odd prime with $μ_p\not\subset K$. For $p\geq 5$, and for $p=3$ under a natural local cyclotomic condition, we prove that every associated finite $A_3$-embedding problem is solvable. In contrast, for every odd $p$ with $μ_p\not\subset K$, we show that no compatible family of finite-stage solutions exists, and hence $C^\bullet(G_K,\mathbb F_p)$ is not genuinely $A_3$-formal. The proof uses Chebotarev density, governing fields, and the Gras-Munnier criterion to obstruct the compatibility of finite-stage solutions, and it builds on previous work of Maire-Mináč-Ramakrishna-Tân. This shows that genuine $A_3$-formality detects a global compatibility obstruction for number fields invisible to every individual finite embedding problem and invisible to obstructions arising from individual strong Massey vanishing problems.

column6: Ray class monoids for orders of number fields
column7: We define and study six ray class monoids associated to a level datum $(\mathcal{O}; \mathfrak{m}, Σ)$, where $\mathcal{O}$ is an order in a number field $K$, $\mathfrak{m}$ is an $\mathcal{O}$-ideal, and $Σ$ is a set of real places of $K$. The monoids extend the ray class group (and the ring class group) by including non-invertible classes consisting of non-invertible ideals and ideals not coprime to the modulus. We prove fundamental results on the structure of these ray class monoids.

column6: Statistics of divisor functions over function fields
column7: Extending recent works on the restricted divisor function over integers, we consider an analogue of this function over the function field. We provide some exact and asymptotic formulas related to this function.

column6: Automorphic symbols and automorphic \emph{L}-values of GL(2) over imaginary quadratic fields
column7: We study non-vanishing modulo primes of critical values of $L$-functions over imaginary quadratic fields twisted by Coates--Wiles characters. For a parallel weight two Hecke eigenform over an imaginary quadratic field, we prove that a positive proportion of Coates--Wiles characters have nonzero integral $L$-values modulo each prime in a positive-density set. The argument constructs automorphic symbols in parabolic homology with integral coefficients and expresses the critical values through their pairings with parabolic cohomology classes. A vertical family of additive averages of these pairings recovers Fourier coefficients and force the module generated by symbols to have full rank. We transfer this full-rank property to non-vanishing modulo primes. This extends the homological strategy of Kim--Sun from classical modular curves to arithmetic orbifolds, while addressing the unit obstructions specific to the imaginary quadratic setting.

column6: Horizontal moments of Kloosterman sums and a density version of sieves
column7: Denote by $\mathrm{Kl}(a,n)$ the normalized Kloosterman sum modulo $n$. In this paper, we study the moments of $|\mathrm{Kl}(1,n)|$ on average over $n\leqslant X$, and show that \begin{align*} \sum_{n\leqslant X}|\mathrm{Kl}(1,n)|\asymp X(\log X)^{\frac{8}{3π}-1}. \end{align*} The lower bound is proven by considering a subfamily of moduli which factorize in a nice way such that vertical Sato--Tate distributions of Kloosterman sums (as variants of Katz) apply. The upper bound is based on a new density version of upper bound sieves, combining with averages of divisor functions in arithmetic progressions and a similar vertical Sato--Tate distribution.

column6: A combinatorial proof of the quadratic Gauss sum
column7: We provide an elementary approach to computing the quadratic Gauss sum, emphasizing the method employed to compute the sum corresponding to multiples of 4. The proof method employed does not rely on the law of quadratic reciprocity, but only on exploiting symmetries among the sum's components, together with a recursive approach.

column6: A note on Riemann's $R$-function and almost primes
column7: The real-axis jump of the prime-zeta function gives an integral form of Gram's series for Riemann's $R$-function. Applying the same operation to the classical almost-prime generating functions defines a smooth family $R_k$, with $R_1=R$. We give the construction and a convergence argument, and explain why its expansion at every fixed logarithmic order is the Selberg--Delange expansion. The distinction lies in the smaller real-axis contributions retained by the definition, rather than in new asymptotic coefficients. A finite Perron decomposition also identifies the additional contour terms required for exact recovery of the count.

column5: Alia Hamieh; Do Nhat Tan Vo
column6: Additive Sums of Generalized Shifted Ternary Divisor Functions
column7: In this paper, we prove a conditional result that yields an asymptotic formula with an explicit main term and a power-saving error term for the generalized shifted ternary additive divisor sum $D_{\mathcal{I},\mathcal{J}}(X,1)=\sum_{n \leq X} τ_{\mathcal{I}}(n) τ_{\mathcal{J}}(n + 1)$, where $\mathcal{I}=\{α_1,α_2,α_3\}$ and $\mathcal{J} = \{β_1, β_2, β_3\}$, with $|α_i|, |β_i|\leq δ$ for $i=1,2,3$, and $0<δ<1/44$. The proof of our main theorem relies on assuming an averaged level of distribution for the generalized ternary additive divisor function $τ_{\mathcal{J}}$ in arithmetic progressions up to the level $2/3$.

column5: Angel Cano; Hector Castro; Nikolay Gusevskii
column6: Splitting fields of complex hyperbolic groups: matrix extraction, Hermitian descent, and spectral fields
column7: Let $Γ<\mathrm{SU}(n,1)$, $n\ge2$, be Zariski-dense and contain a regular loxodromic element $A$. The splitting-field problem asks how far traces and spectra determine a field of definition for $Γ$. We show first that traces together with the spectrum of $A$ always give a linear realization over $K=\mathbb{Q}(\textrm{tr}Γ,E(A))$. We also prove that every complex-irreducible subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(n,1)$ with real trace field is conjugate into $\mathrm{SO}(n,1)$; in particular, no discreteness hypothesis is required for this real-trace conclusion. In higher dimension, however, linear descent does not by itself give the standard unitary form: a Hermitian similarity obstruction remains, described over imaginary quadratic fields by Landherr's local invariants. In $\mathrm{SU}(3,1)$ we give a Zariski-dense example for which the one-spectrum field is $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ but does not yield the standard unitary form. This leads naturally to the total spectral field. We prove that the obstruction disappears for arithmetic groups and under suitable local openness hypotheses, and we give an even-degree local criterion. In dimension four we analyze the discrete branch through explicit Schottky groups and rank-one local geometry. There the full Bruhat cocycle recovers anisotropic Levi holonomy and forces a non-split rotational word. The remaining quasi-split rank-two case is not reached by this method, so the general $\mathrm{SU}(3,1)$ problem remains open.

column6: Equidistribution of number theoretic point sets in the torus and the sphere in Wasserstein metric and $L^2$ discrepancy
column7: We find the exact rate of equidistribution of several arithmetic point configurations in Wasserstein metric and $L^2$ discrepancy with respect to balls. Kronecker sequences in the torus and the Fibonacci lattice on the Euclidean unit sphere are shown to be more evenly distributed in Wasserstein metric than random points. Modular hyperbolas and modular parabolas in the torus behave like random points, although the constants in the asymptotics of the $L^2$ discrepancy with respect to balls differ from the random case. We also prove a sharp inequality between the quadratic Wasserstein metric and the $L^2$ discrepancy with respect to balls for an arbitrary probability measure on the torus or the sphere. In particular, we show that any point set that is optimally close to the uniform measure in $L^2$ discrepancy with respect to balls is also optimal in the quadratic Wasserstein metric.

column6: Non-degeneracy and Fibering with Applications to Diophantine Approximation
column7: Motivated by applications in Diophantine approximation, we develop a new fibering mechanism for non-degenerate manifolds in $\mathbb{R}^n$, showing that they admit local decompositions into families of non-degenerate curves with uniform quantitative non-degeneracy properties. The manifolds are required to be $C^N$ with the essentially optimal bound $N\geq \max\lbrace n,l+1\rbrace$, where the manifold is $l$ non-degenerate. Furthermore, we show that this uniform quantitative local control can be globalised into a qualitative statement, so that almost every point of a non-degenerate manifold lies on a non-degenerate curve contained in the manifold. Our approach is perturbative and shows that the fibering structure arising in the analytic setting is stable under sufficiently small $C^N$ perturbations. The method provides a framework for extending fibering based results in Diophantine approximation from curves to manifolds. Such applications are considered in the paper.

column6: K-moduli wall crossing for quasimaps to a projective variety
column7: We develop a modular wall crossing theory for quasimaps to a projective variety, allowing independent variation of the boundary coefficients and the quasimap weight. Building on the K-stability of quasimaps introduced by Hashizume and the first author, we construct projective moduli spaces in the stable, Calabi--Yau, and log Fano regimes, together with wall crossing morphisms. A central construction is the moduli theory of boundary polarized Calabi--Yau quasimaps, which retains an ample polarization at the numerically trivial locus and allows comparison with suitable perturbations toward the stable and log Fano regions. The stable theory applies in arbitrary genus, while the comparisons through the Calabi--Yau locus concern genus zero. For degree-one boundary divisors, the resulting framework relates weighted stable maps and quasimaps to Hassett spaces and GIT quotients of weighted points on $\mathbb P^1$. In a companion paper, we apply this framework to give a modular interpolation between Miranda's GIT compactification of rational elliptic surfaces and the Baily--Borel compactification of an eight-dimensional ball quotient.

column6: K-Moduli Wall Crossing and Automorphic Forms for the Moduli Space of Rational Elliptic Surfaces
column7: Using K-moduli spaces for log quasimaps $q_t\colon\left(\mathbb P^1,\frac{1-t}{12}D\right)\to[\mathbb A^2/\mathbb G_m]$ of degree twelve with twelve points and weight $t/12$, we construct a modular interpolation $\{\mathcal M_t\}_{0\le t\le1}$ between the Baily--Borel compactification of the Heckman--Looijenga ball quotient $X_o$ and Miranda's GIT compactification of the moduli space of rational elliptic surfaces. We completely determine the wall-crossing and, for every rational $t\in[0,1]$, identify \[ \mathcal M_t\cong\operatorname{Proj}R\!\left(X_o,\mathcal L+\frac t2Δ(6)+\frac t3Δ(9)\right), \] where $\mathcal L$ is the automorphic $\mathbb Q$-line bundle and $Δ(6),Δ(9)$ are distinguished Heegner divisors. On the automorphic side, we construct a new automorphic form on $X_o$ via a Borcherds product, whose divisor gives an independent relation among the Heegner divisors. This relation provides a key input for determining the birational transformations in the K-moduli wall-crossing. As part of this analysis, we show that the first positive chamber $\mathcal M_t$ for $t\in (0,1/7)$ is Looijenga's semi-toroidal compactification.

column6: Cardinalities of Jordan Diophantine sets of upper triangular integer matrices
column7: Let $U$ be the ring of upper triangular $2\times2$ integer matrices. For $N\in U$, a Jordan $D(N)$-set is a set of distinct nonzero matrices in $U$ such that $(AB+BA)/2+N$ is a square in $U$ for any two distinct elements $A$ and $B$. We determine all $N$ for which an infinite Jordan $D(N)$-set exists. If no infinite set exists, every such set has at most six elements. If $N$ is not a difference of two squares in $U$, the bound is five. Both bounds are best possible. We also give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of infinite sets with nonzero pairwise Jordan products and of infinite sets consisting of nonsingular matrices.

column6: Long intervals of consecutive composite values of polynomials
column7: Let $f\in\mathbb Q[t]$ be an irreducible integer-valued polynomial of positive degree with positive leading coefficient. We show that there is a constant $c_f>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large real $X$, the interval $(X/2,X]$ contains a block of at least $c_f\log X\log\log X$ consecutive integers $n$ for which $f(n)$ is composite. The exponent of $\log\log X$ does not depend on the degree of $f$. This improves a result of Ford and Gabdullin, replacing a small fixed power of $\log\log X$ by $\log\log X$. The result includes the case $f(t)=t^2+1$.

column6: On Densities in the Erdős-Falconer Distance Problems over the Integers
column7: Motivated by the classical Erdős and Falconer distance problems and Magyar's work on distance sets in $\mathbb Z^d$, we study discrete analogues of the Erdős-Falconer unpinned and pinned distance problems over the integers. We ask how the discrete Hausdorff dimension of a set $A\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ influences the size of its squared-distance sets, measured by generalized upper natural density and upper discrete mass dimension. We propose conjectures for both problems and prove the unpinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2,3$ and the pinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2$. For the unpinned problem in higher dimensions, we obtain explicit lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets using elementary integer sphere counting, results on the Erdős distinct distances problem, and $\ell^p$-improving inequalities for discrete spherical averages. For the pinned problem, we obtain lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets for some or every pin. We also establish more general results involving upper discrete mass dimension, upper discrete Banach dimension, and affine dimension, including bounds on the affine dimension of the exceptional set of pins.
